title: Goblin Deal
description: A negotiation ritual for shiny distractions that lets you bargain with the craving instead of pretending it does not exist.
heroIntro: A negotiation ritual for shiny distractions. Use it when the boring task keeps losing the auction to whatever feels more stimulating right now.
howToUse: Name the distraction out loud. Writing it down takes away half its power.
Pre-choose the reward: a snack, a scroll, a song, a stretch. Decide now, not later.
Set a short timer (15-25 minutes). Work the boring task until it rings.
When the timer rings, take the reward. Fully. No guilt. Then decide: another round or done.
whyItHelps: It stops the craving from being the villain and makes it part of the contract.
It gives the brain a concrete finish line instead of open-ended suffering.
It adds friction to the impulse without pretending the impulse is fake.
minimalPrompt:
Goblin Deal
The shiny thing: ___________________________
The boring task: ___________________________
Pre-chosen reward: ___________________________
Timer: ___ minutes
Deal struck: yes / no

title: Minimum Viable Day
description: A survival ritual for burnout that shrinks the day to its true essentials before you try to plan anything else.
heroIntro: A survival ritual for burnout. Use it when everything costs too much and the honest answer is a smaller day, not a better attitude.
oath: I will name what must happen. Everything else is optional until proven otherwise.
One recovery action goes on the list before a single new task does.
howToUse: List only what truly must happen today. If it can wait until tomorrow without real consequences, it waits.
Add one recovery action to the list: a nap, a walk, a meal, silence. It is not optional.
Cross off anything you added from habit, guilt, or fantasy fuel.
Do the surviving list in any order. Stop when it is done.
whyItHelps: It matches the plan to the actual fuel supply instead of yesterday's capacity.
It protects recovery from being the first thing cut.
It lets you finish a day instead of failing a bigger one.
minimalPrompt:
Minimum Viable Day
Must happen: [   ] [   ] [   ]
Recovery action: ___________________________
Cut from habit/guilt: ___________________________
When the list is done, I stop.

title: Reduce Inputs First
description: A sensory triage ritual that cuts stimuli before adding tools, because your brain needs less before it needs more.
heroIntro: A sensory triage ritual for overload. Use it when sound, light, and texture are piling up and your brain needs less input before it can do anything else.
howToUse: Name the loudest, brightest, scratchiest, or most socially demanding input right now.
Lower or remove that one thing. Headphones off, lights down, door closed, notification silenced.
Give your body one steady anchor: cold water, pressure, a single calm sound, or dimmer light.
Wait two minutes. Then ask what your brain can handle from here.
whyItHelps: It treats overload as an input problem, not a willpower problem.
It works faster than any strategy that adds more things to manage.
It gives the nervous system room to come back online before you ask it to perform.
minimalPrompt:
Reduce Inputs First
Loudest input right now: ___________________________
Action to lower it: ___________________________
One-sense anchor: ___________________________
After 2 min, I can handle: ___________________________

title: Reply Scaffold
description: A pre-written response ritual for rejection sensitivity that gives you reply shapes before the flood hits.
heroIntro: A pre-written response ritual for rejection sensitivity. Use it when one hard message has turned the whole inbox into a minefield.
howToUse: Pick one reply shape: acknowledge, yes, no, or clarify.
Fill the slots with the minimum honest words. No backstory, no apology tour.
Read it once for facts. If the facts are right, send it.
Close the thread. You replied. The rest is not your job right now.
whyItHelps: It removes the blank-page problem from emotional replies.
It separates "what do I say" from "what does this mean about me."
It lets you act before the Wisp finishes narrating.
minimalPrompt:
Reply Scaffold
Shape: acknowledge / yes / no / clarify
Slot 1 (the fact): ___________________________
Slot 2 (the action): ___________________________
Read once for facts: done / not yet
Send.

title: Single-Task Oath
description: A short ritual for overwhelm spirals that helps you name one task, stay in one lane, and stop the list from multiplying.
heroIntro: A short ritual for overwhelm spirals. Use it when the list keeps multiplying and you need one visible task instead of ten competing ones.
oath: I choose one head. I do not grow new ones.
Today's three quests are visible. The rest can wait.
howToUse: Name one task, not an entire project category.
Gather only the tools that belong to that task.
Put every new idea in a parking lot instead of promoting it into the current battle.
Finish, stop, and choose again.
whyItHelps: It reduces switching costs.
It creates an external rule before overwhelm starts negotiating.
It keeps new ideas from hijacking the current lane.
minimalPrompt:
Single-Task Oath
I choose one head. I do not grow new ones.
Today's three quests: [   ] [   ] [   ]
Parking lot: ___________________________

title: Threshold Spell
description: A micro-transition ritual for shutdown and retreat that helps you cross one doorway before your brain asks for the whole plan.
heroIntro: A micro-transition ritual for shutdown and retreat. Use it when the cave feels safer than the world and you need one doorway, not an expedition.
howToUse: Stand in a literal or figurative doorway: the bedroom door, the reply button, the first sentence of the email.
Take three slow breaths in the threshold.
Make three small moves: sit up, feet on floor, stand. Or: open app, read one line, type one word.
From the doorway, decide: one more step, or rest here. Either answer is legal.
whyItHelps: It shrinks the ask from "rejoin the world" to "reach the door."
It uses body movement to interrupt the freeze loop.
It gives you a decision point after motion, not before it.
minimalPrompt:
Threshold Spell
Doorway I am crossing: ___________________________
Three breaths: done / not yet
Three moves: [   ] [   ] [   ]
From the doorway: one more step / rest here

heroIntro: A pre-commitment ritual for time blindness. Use it when deadlines feel imaginary until they are suddenly on top of you.
whyItHelps: It turns intention into a visible commitment.
It reduces the gap between "I should" and "I am starting now."
It gives the brain something concrete before panic takes over.

title: Ugly First Pass
description: A counter-spell for perfectionism loops that gives you permission to make the whole shape badly before polishing anything.
heroIntro: A counter-spell for perfectionism loops. Use it when the Wyrm whispers that the draft is not ready and you know it never will be.
oath: My first job is existence, not elegance.
I will make the whole shape before I polish any sentence.
howToUse: Set a timer for the entire draft, not the first section.
Write every section as bullet points, placeholders, or garbage prose. All of it counts.
Mark anything that feels wrong with [FIX LATER] and keep moving.
When the timer ends, you have a full ugly shape. Now you may polish.
whyItHelps: It separates creation from editing, which use different brain modes.
It removes the Wyrm's leverage: you cannot endlessly revise what does not exist yet.
It makes "done" visible before "perfect" gets a vote.
minimalPrompt:
Ugly First Pass
My first job is existence, not elegance.
Sections to rough out: [   ] [   ] [   ] [   ]
[FIX LATER] count: ___
Ship line: when __________ is done, I send it.

heroIntro: A bedside ritual for hard starts. Use it when mornings become negotiations before your feet hit the floor.
whyItHelps: It reduces morning decision load.
It uses body cues instead of waiting for motivation.
It makes the first movement feel smaller and more scripted.
